CompanyIn.description:
Create an account. `owner_id` must resolve to a rep in this organization's
directory (`GET /customers/owners`). `annual_revenue_minor` is integer minor units of
`currency`; no float is accepted on this path.
CompanyIn.title: CompanyIn

CompanyOut.description:
Mirrors the SPA's `Company`. `annual_revenue_minor` is minor units of `currency`;
`size_band` is a display band ("201-500"), not a number.
CompanyOut.title: CompanyOut

CompanyPatch.description:
Partial update. Absent means "leave alone"; every field is the same shape as
`CompanyIn`, just optional.
CompanyPatch.title: CompanyPatch

ContactIn.description:
Add a person to an account. Deliberately **no `phone` field** — the mask is a
server-derived projection and must never be writable. Give a real number, if there is
one, through `raw_phone`; it is sealed and the mask derived from it (see
`services.create_contact`). `extra="forbid"` so a caller can never smuggle `phone` in.
ContactIn.title: ContactIn

ContactOut.description:
Mirrors the SPA's `Contact`. `phone` is the masked read shape the service returns by
default; `last_activity_at` is NULL for a contact never touched.
ContactOut.title: ContactOut

ContactPatch.description:
Partial update of the plain contact fields. Deliberately **no `phone`, no
`raw_phone`** — the number stays on its own dedicated route
(`PUT /contacts/{id}/phone`), so a masked value can never be written back over a
sealed one and a PATCH can never smuggle a raw number in unaudited.
ContactPatch.title: ContactPatch

ContactPhoneIn.description: Set a contact's real number. The mask is derived from it, never supplied.
ContactPhoneIn.title: ContactPhoneIn

ContactPhoneRevealed.description:
A contact's real number, revealed to a human who stepped up.

Returned only by the dedicated unmask route, which requires the dangerous
`read_sensitive` permission and a second factor, and which writes an audit row every time.
`phone` is None when the contact has no sealed number.
ContactPhoneRevealed.title: ContactPhoneRevealed

OwnerIn.description:
Add a rep to the directory. A production org starts with zero owners, and every
company / contact / deal create needs an `owner_id`, so this is the first write.
OwnerIn.title: OwnerIn

OwnerOut.description:
Mirrors the SPA's `Owner`. The `id` is what every `owner_id` in the product carries,
including deal-service's — the SPA resolves display names from this list client-side.
OwnerOut.title: OwnerOut

OwnerPatch.description:
Edit a rep, or deactivate one. Absent means "leave alone". Setting `is_active` to
`False` is the deactivation path (`services.deactivate_owner`) and refuses while the rep
still owns a live company or contact — reassign those first.
OwnerPatch.title: OwnerPatch

info.description: Customer service — part of the OpsGrids platform.
info.title: Customer service

post.summary: Add a contact to an account

put.description:
Seal a real number onto a contact and derive its mask.

Returns the ordinary `ContactOut` — the masked form — so the write surface cannot be used
as a read-back oracle for the number just supplied. Revealing it needs the separate
stepped-up route below.
put.summary: Set a contact's real phone number

post.description:
The only public route that returns a real number.

A POST rather than a GET on purpose: this has a side effect — it writes an
`entity.sensitive_read` audit row — and it must never be cached, pre-fetched, logged in a
query string or replayed from browser history the way a GET can be.

Guarded by the dangerous `read_sensitive` permission and a second factor, then re-scoped
to this one contact. Filtering a list and forgetting the detail route is the named
vulnerability this shape exists to avoid.
post.summary: Reveal a contact's real phone number (audited)
Add a company to the account book

get.description:
A plain array, not a page: the SPA loads the whole directory once and resolves
`owner_id` values client-side. Reference data within the organization, so it is
org-scoped but not scope-narrowed — a name must resolve on any row a caller sees.

schema.title: Response List Owners Api V1 Customers Owners Get

get.summary: The rep directory — who owner_id values resolve to

post.description:
The prerequisite for everything else: a production org starts with zero owners,
and every company / contact / deal create needs an `owner_id` that resolves to one.
post.summary: Add a rep to the directory

patch.description:
One route for both edits and deactivation, distinguished by whether `is_active` is
present. Deactivating refuses (409) while the rep still owns a live company or contact —
reassign first. Reactivating has no such guard: a returning rep starts with an empty
book.
patch.summary: Edit a rep, or deactivate one

get.description:
Sections that cannot be produced are `null` and named in `unavailable`; the response is
still 200. Only the contact itself decides 404.

Route traffic on this; restart on /health.

Conflating the two restarts a healthy process that is merely waiting on a
dependency.

Only the dependencies a service actually declares are checked. A gateway owns no
tables, so asking it for a database is asking a question whose answer means nothing
— and a readiness probe that reports on something the service does not use is worse
than no probe, because it will eventually fail for a reason nobody can act on.

Reachable only on the compose `back` network (`tests/infra`'s
`test_metrics_never_routed.py` is the lint that keeps it that way) — never behind
Caddy or a gateway, the same rule `ops_monitor`'s own `/metrics` follows.

`db_pool_in_use` is always reported when this service has a database; the three
outbox gauges only when `outbox_model` is configured — same gate as `/health/outbox`,
and the same reason: an app-role connection with no tenant bound sees zero rows.
